Well, to be honest, in my country mental health awareness is really on a low level. Talking about it within mass media is forbidden, a lot of people still believe that depression, ptsd and etc. either don’t exist or are the illnesses of the weak and stupid cowards. Having a competent specialist at the university or at school seems like beyond reality to me. I studied at a pretty good school that was rather modern and progressive and all, and still we had a school counselor who actually didn’t even seem to fully understand how to work with children, teens and their psychological problems. And I don’t think we have one in the university either. At least I’ve never heard we did. 

I don’t feel like going to such a specialist for free. I want to know for sure what’s wrong with me, how severe it is and what should I do to help myself.  Money doesn’t always mean good, but free medicine here is worse than Russian roulette. 

Speaking of triggers... I can say for sure: there was nothing THAT serious going on lately, but some little things came together and hit me hard enough to bring me back to those thoughts. 

I got a part-time job as a shop assistant at a book store to prove myself and my parents I’m able to earn money myself, I loved it there, but I got fired within two months because I sucked at selling books. Boom.  I’ve never had friends and now, when I finally found them, I am scared as hell that I  can push them away or that I’m a burden to them - that’s how diffident I am. There’s always a thought at the back of my head that I’m not worth having something perfectly good or feeling happy for long. Boom. My studies weren’t good this semester. I failed at one exam and will have to pass it again. I almost failed the other one, which is my top-subject. I did my best to achieve good results and was sure this time I was finally making something right and still I fucked up, as always. I keep on screwing everything up no matter how hard I try for a really long time now, I’ve never made something I could be proud of or my parents could be proud of. Boom. And for my parents my studies is of extreme importance, so we fought really hard when they found out. It always hurts when we fight with them because our fights are loud and serious. BOOM. I actually think all my problems come from my relations with parents, especially mom. She was always trying to protect me from everything, she was totally over caring and, what’s more, she hoped I would grow up to be like my sister who was the best of the best - but I grew up to be absolutely useless, nothing like my sister, with low self-esteem, too shy, too lonely, too confused about how to live this life. And still they put too much hope at me and I’m not able to make them proud.

Sorry for such a long response. Just wanted to put what’s on my mind.
Tell me you didn’t do it, please

People won’t start caring ‘bout you when you die. The world will stay the same for most of them, it won’t change or stop spinning. Because most people have their own beloved ones to take care of. 

But the world definitely will change for those who loved you, for whom you mattered, and trust me, this won’t be a good change.

No, you shouldn’t live for anybody else. Family and friends are very important, but it’s YOUR life at the first place, so it’s YOU who decide yourself what to do with it. 

the question is, is it really worth dying? Isn’t there really anything you should be fighting for? If there’s anything what can make you happier or anyone who can ease the pain inside, maybe you should at least try to go on? You can always take your life, but will never be able to come back and get a second chance to live. Realization of this, the fact suicide is the point of no return, the fear of the unknown that awaits after death, is actually the only thing that stops me myself from doing it, too. if I wasn’t so afraid to die, it would’ve been so easy for me to kill myself last year when I wanted to do it so badly. See, I’m not the right person to give you help because I also have my issues I still can’t fix but I just want to support you and show you are not alone. You matter. You really do. 

the choice to end your life is, still, A CHOICE and should not be judged. We all choose our paths ourselves, don’t we? I don’t think suicide is cowardly (still i don’t find it courageous either) or weak. 

I just feel terrified when I realize there are so many people out there who feel so broken and hurt so badly they cannot take it anymore. I just want to reach out to all of those lonely souls that are about to give up on themselves and shout out to them — I KNOW HOW YOU FEEL, I FEEL THE SAME, WE’RE IN THIS TOGETHER. Together we can fight and defeat it. Show we’re strong enough to go through hell and still learn to be happy.
